lead: The 2020s are set to be the worst decade for real income growth since 1950.
The government is still on course to run a current budget surplus by 2029-30, but smaller, and with more of the fall in borrowing in later years.
Faced with a worse forecast, the Chancellor has chosen to allow borrowing to increase, which leaves him less scope to absorb bad news in future.
OBR expects growth to slow significantly in 2027, but by 2030-31 they expect the level of GDP to fully catch up with their expectations from March.
OBR forecasts household disposable incomes to grow by 0.4% per year during this parliament, making it the second worst of any parliament since 1979.
Today's Budget will increase the overall tax take by around 0.2% of GDP: much smaller increases than the previous two Budgets of this parliament.
The OBR now forecasts 10.8 million people will pay the higher or additional rate of income tax by March 2031.
